question.worked_solution:
Interpreting the fractions as division, we get

$$
(9\,÷\,2)\times (8\,÷\,3).
$$

 

Since our expression contains multiplication and division only, we can create an equivalent expression by swapping the $÷\,2$ and $÷\,3$:

 

$$
(9\,÷\,3)\times (8\,÷\,2)
$$

 

Interpreting the divisions as fractions, we get

$$
\frac{9}{3}\times \frac{8}{2}.
$$

Carrying out the divisions, we arrive at

$$
\begin{aligned}{{\frac{9}{3}}_{⏟}}_{3}\times {{\frac{8}{2}}_{⏟}}_{4}=3\times 4=12.\end{aligned}
$$
